title: Father John Bocage, boat builder, and French ancestry
summary: His father built boats and played a little guitar; uncles Paul and Feast; the grandfather came from France. Bocage never learned French.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: And was your father a musician?

Well, my father was a boat builder. He, uh... built boats. Mm-hmm. Of course he... My father played a little music too at the time, but his... Most of his work was boat building. He built boats. Mm-hmm. What was his name? Yeah. His name was John Bocage. Mm-hmm. And did, uh...
What about his brothers? Did they play music?
Well, no. All his brothers are dead out. He had one brother named Paul, and another brother named Feast. Well, they all dead. My father and all of them died out. Feast, his name was?
Yeah.
Do you know how you spell that?
Feast, Bocage.
Do you know how to spell it?
Oh, how? Do you know how to spell it? I don't know how to spell Feast.
Feast? F-E-I-C-E. That's the only way I know how to spell it.
Yeah. Yeah. Well, I just never had heard the name, you know. I suppose it's a French name. Must be French.
Yeah, it was all French. You see, my father... Mm-hmm. Otherwise, my grandfather came from France.
Mm-hmm.
And my daddy, he brought my daddy over here as a kid.
Mm-hmm.
Because, uh, when my boy went into the service, uh, they had a street in France by the name of the Bocage.
Oh, really?
Yeah. They named the street over there after.
Do you speak French?
Yeah.
Yourself?
Who, me?
Do you talk any French?

No, I never talked it. My father and all of them talked it, but I used to laugh at them. In other words, I was foolish not to learn it, because they used to all talk it and I'd laugh. My mother could talk it, my father could talk it, but I never did bother but learn it.
